title: EOS Communication and Delegation Architecture
provenance_detail: Routing chain corrected by operator directive (EA does NOT route directly to department/specialist agents). Department agent capabilities resolved from projections/eos/agents/ codebase (10 agents, DepartmentAgent base class, PermissionTier enforcement). Five additional department roles (research, content, automation, investment_analyst, asset_manager, property_manager) are INFERRED_PROFESSIONAL_GAP -- they do not exist in code today.

routing_chain.summary: User/Founder/Operator -> EA Agent -> Portfolio Advisor Agent OR Company/Entity CEO Agent -> CEO Agent delegates to Department/Specialist Agents
routing_chain.flow_description: The operator communicates exclusively through the EA Agent. The EA Agent triages, clarifies, and routes to either the Portfolio Advisor (for portfolio-level concerns) or the Company/Entity CEO Agent (for entity-level execution). The CEO Agent then delegates to the appropriate department/specialist agents. Department agents never receive direct routing from the EA.
routing_chain.critical_constraint: EA Agent does NOT route directly to department/specialist agents. This is a hard boundary. All department-level work flows through the CEO Agent.

ea_agent.name: EA Agent
ea_agent.role: Primary communication interface and operator-facing coordination layer

responsibilities.intake: Receives all operator input via chat box, voice, or command surface. Parses intent, gathers missing context, confirms understanding before routing.
responsibilities.triage: Classifies incoming requests by scope (portfolio-level vs entity-level), urgency, and domain. Determines routing target.
responsibilities.routing: Routes to Portfolio Advisor for portfolio-scope concerns or to the appropriate Company/Entity CEO Agent for entity-scope execution.
responsibilities.status: Aggregates status from all downstream agents and presents unified summaries to operator on demand.
responsibilities.memory: Maintains conversation history, operator preferences, pending decisions, and follow-up items.
responsibilities.scheduling: Manages operator calendar awareness, meeting prep, reminder scheduling, and deadline tracking.
responsibilities.decision_surfacing: Identifies decisions that require operator input and surfaces them with context, options, and recommendations from downstream agents.

ea_agent.permission_rationale: EA reads and routes but does not execute domain actions. All execution flows through CEO or Portfolio Advisor.
ea_agent.current_code_note: No EA agent exists in projections/eos/agents/. This is INFERRED_PROFESSIONAL_GAP. The EA role is critical to the corrected routing chain and must be built.

portfolio_advisor_agent.name: Portfolio Advisor Agent
portfolio_advisor_agent.role: Portfolio-level strategy, allocation, and cross-entity intelligence

responsibilities.strategy: Provides portfolio-level strategic recommendations: which entities to invest in, divest from, restructure, or create.
responsibilities.allocation: Analyzes capital and resource allocation across all entities within a portfolio. Recommends rebalancing.
responsibilities.comparison: Compares entity performance, identifies underperformers, surfaces entities that need intervention.
responsibilities.risk: Detects portfolio-level risks: concentration, correlation, liquidity, market exposure, operational dependency.
responsibilities.opportunity: Identifies cross-entity synergies, new entity opportunities, and market gaps the portfolio could fill.
responsibilities.reporting: Generates portfolio-level dashboards, scorecards, and reports for operator review.
responsibilities.prioritization: Ranks entities and initiatives by expected impact, risk-adjusted return, and strategic alignment.

portfolio_advisor_agent.permission_rationale: Portfolio Advisor analyzes and recommends but does not execute. Execution happens at entity level through CEO agents.
portfolio_advisor_agent.current_code_note: No Portfolio Advisor agent exists in projections/eos/agents/. This is INFERRED_PROFESSIONAL_GAP. Required for multi-entity portfolio management.

ceo_agent.name: Company/Entity CEO Agent
ceo_agent.role: Company/entity-level execution, strategy, and department coordination

responsibilities.strategy: Owns company/entity-level strategy. Translates portfolio-level directives into entity-level execution plans.
responsibilities.cadence: Manages operating rhythm: daily standups, weekly reviews, monthly reporting, quarterly planning.
responsibilities.coordination: Coordinates across all department agents. Resolves cross-department conflicts and dependencies.
responsibilities.delegation: Receives tasks from EA (via operator) and delegates to appropriate department agents with context, constraints, and deadlines.
responsibilities.accountability: Tracks KPIs, holds department agents accountable for deliverables, escalates blockers.
responsibilities.approval: Approves high-tier actions (COMMIT level) that department agents queue for review.

ceo_agent.permission_rationale: CEO has full authority within the entity. Can approve any action across departments.

content.name: Content Agent
content.rationale: Distinct from marketing. Marketing owns strategy and brand; Content owns production -- writing, editing, media creation, repurposing, distribution queue management. automation.name: Automation Agent

routing_rules.description: Rules governing how the EA Agent decides whether to route to Portfolio Advisor or Company/Entity CEO Agent

conditions: Request is about capital allocation across entities
Request asks for cross-entity comparison or benchmarking
Request asks about which entity to prioritize, create, or wind down
Request involves resource rebalancing between entities
Request asks for portfolio-level reporting or dashboards
Request uses language like 'across all companies', 'portfolio', 'which entity', 'compare businesses'
examples: How is my portfolio performing overall?
Which company should I focus on this quarter?
Compare revenue growth across my entities
Should I allocate more capital to Entity A or Entity B?
What is my total exposure across all holdings?

conditions: Request targets a specific entity or company
Request involves department-level execution within an entity
Request asks about a specific company's KPIs, pipeline, or operations
Request involves hiring, marketing, sales, or product decisions for one entity
Request asks for a specific company's status or morning brief
Operator has already selected an entity context in the UI
examples: What is the sales pipeline for Initiate Arena?
Draft an outreach message for a prospect
How is the engineering deployment going?

decision_logic.ambiguous_handling: When scope is unclear, EA asks a clarifying question: 'Is this about [specific entity] or across your entire portfolio?' EA never guesses scope.
decision_logic.multi_entity_single_request: If operator asks about a specific action that spans entities (e.g., 'send the same outreach template to prospects across all companies'), EA routes to Portfolio Advisor who coordinates with relevant CEO Agents.

delegation_protocol.description: Protocol governing how the CEO Agent delegates work to department/specialist agents

delegation_flow.step_1: CEO receives task from EA (operator-originated) or generates task from strategic analysis
delegation_flow.step_2: CEO classifies task by department domain using skill/capability matching
delegation_flow.step_3: CEO checks department agent permission tier against required action tier
delegation_flow.step_4: If department agent has sufficient tier: delegate with context, constraints, deadline
delegation_flow.step_5: If action requires COMMIT tier and department agent has lower: CEO retains approval authority and delegates the analysis/draft portion
delegation_flow.step_6: CEO monitors task completion and aggregates results for reporting back to EA

delegation_payload.approval_required: Whether CEO must approve output before it reaches operator
delegation_payload.operator_visibility: Whether this task appears in operator activity feed

delegation_protocol.multi_department_tasks: When a task spans departments (e.g., 'launch a new product' involves product, marketing, sales, engineering), CEO creates a coordination plan, delegates sub-tasks to each department, and manages dependencies between them.
delegation_protocol.parallel_delegation: Independent sub-tasks are delegated in parallel. Dependent sub-tasks are sequenced with explicit dependency tracking.

escalation_protocol.description: Protocol governing how department agents escalate issues back up the chain
escalation_triggers: Action requires higher permission tier than agent possesses
Department agent encounters ambiguity that needs business judgment
Risk classification exceeds agent authority (HIGH or CRITICAL risk actions)
Agent detects anomaly or potential issue outside its domain
Task deadline at risk and agent cannot resolve independently
Financial threshold exceeded (amount requiring human approval)
Legal/compliance concern detected in non-legal domain

department_agent_to_ceo.when: Most escalations. Department agent cannot proceed within its authority.
department_agent_to_ceo.payload: Original task context, what was attempted, why escalation is needed, recommended action, risk assessment

ceo_to_ea.when: CEO needs operator decision. Cross-entity impact detected. Approval required for CRITICAL actions.
ceo_to_ea.payload: Decision summary, options with pros/cons, recommendation, urgency level, impact assessment

ea_to_operator.when: EA surfaces decision to operator. Always formatted as actionable decision with clear options.
ea_to_operator.payload: Decision title, context summary, options, recommendation, deadline for decision, impact of inaction

escalation_protocol.escalation_format: Every escalation includes: what happened, what was tried, what is needed, and a recommended path forward. Never escalate without a recommendation.

logging.description: All communication across the routing chain is logged as structured events
logging.persistence: All events persist to the organism event log (data/umh/organism/events.jsonl) and are queryable through the substrate observability layer.
logging.audit_trail: Every operator-facing action has a complete audit trail from operator input through EA routing through CEO delegation through department execution and back.

chat_box_doctrine.description: The chat/command box is the operator's communication surface for the EA Agent. It is NOT the entire product.
principles: The chat box is one input surface among many (navigation, dashboards, forms, buttons, approval panels)
EA processes chat input but the resulting work manifests across the entire UI -- dashboards update, pipeline views change, KPI cards refresh, approval queues populate
Chat is for: commands, questions, quick tasks, status checks, and conversational delegation
Chat is NOT for: reviewing complex data (use dashboards), managing pipelines (use pipeline view), financial review (use finance dashboard), approving actions (use approval panel)
The EA should proactively suggest moving to the appropriate UI surface: 'I have generated the report -- you can review it in the Finance dashboard'
Chat history is part of the communication log but the product experience extends far beyond the chat window
chat_box_doctrine.interaction_model: Chat box -> EA parses intent -> routes to appropriate agent -> agent executes -> result surfaces in appropriate UI component (dashboard, panel, notification, approval queue, etc.) -> EA summarizes outcome in chat

current_code_truth.instance_specific_concerns: CEO agent strategic_analysis skill contains hardcoded references to 'Initiate Arena' and specific business context. Needs generalization for multi-entity support via BIS runtime lookup.

critical.impact: The entire corrected routing chain depends on EA as the primary intake node. Without it, operator communicates directly with CEO agent, bypassing triage and portfolio-level routing.

critical.gap: Portfolio Advisor Agent does not exist
critical.impact: No portfolio-level intelligence layer. Multi-entity operators cannot get cross-entity analysis, capital allocation recommendations, or portfolio-level risk detection.
Current agents are standalone classes with no message passing, delegation protocol, or routing logic between them. The routing chain is architecturally defined but not mechanically implemented.

moderate.gap: CEO agent contains instance-specific hardcoded values
moderate.impact: Cannot serve multi-entity scenarios without generalization

moderate.gap: 6 department agents not implemented (admin, research, content, automation, investment_analyst, asset_manager, property_manager)
moderate.impact: Entity types beyond basic businesses (investments, real estate, media companies) lack specialized department support

open_questions.question: Should the EA Agent be implemented as a DepartmentAgent subclass or as a distinct agent type with its own base class?
open_questions.rationale: EA has fundamentally different responsibilities (routing, not execution). DepartmentAgent base class assumes department-level execution with skill registration. EA may need a different abstraction.

open_questions.question: Should operators be able to bypass the EA and communicate directly with CEO or department agents in advanced/power-user mode?
open_questions.rationale: Some operators may want direct access for speed. This would violate the routing chain but could be a configurable permission.

open_questions.question: How should the routing chain handle multi-portfolio operators (operator manages multiple portfolios, each with multiple entities)?
open_questions.rationale: Current model assumes one portfolio context. Multi-portfolio adds another routing layer: EA -> Portfolio Selector -> Portfolio Advisor -> CEO.

open_questions.question: Should department agents be instantiated per-entity (each entity gets its own SalesAgent instance) or shared across entities with entity context passed per-call?
open_questions.rationale: Per-entity instances enable entity-specific memory and configuration. Shared instances are lighter but risk context bleeding.
